question: Should OpenClaw core accept a public `openclaw catalog` CLI, plugin descriptor metadata, and prompt overlay contract now, and should it land as this broad draft or as smaller reviewed slices?
rationale: The unresolved choice is product/API scope, not a mechanical bug fix: the PR creates new user-facing CLI output, plugin-author metadata, and model-visible prompt behavior.

options.title: Sponsor A Narrowed Contract
options.body: Approve the direction but require a split or narrowed stack with real CLI proof, compatibility review, and owner-approved contract boundaries before merge.

options.title: Keep It As RFC For Now
options.body: Use this PR for design discussion and wait for the RFC/node-operator consumers to settle before merging OpenClaw core changes.

options.title: Land This Broad Stack After Fixes
options.body: Keep this PR as the landing vehicle once proof, mergeability, and owner review are complete, accepting the larger review surface.

recommendation.title: Sponsor A Narrowed Contract
recommendation.body: Approve the direction but require a split or narrowed stack with real CLI proof, compatibility review, and owner-approved contract boundaries before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This spans product direction plus public CLI/plugin/prompt contracts, making the project-level direction owner the best available decision route.
